      <title>Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza cleared of using AI to write prize-winning story</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/books/2026/nov/12/zimbabwean-author-simbarashe-kundizeza-cleared-ai-caine-prize-winning-story</link>
      <description><p>After a month-long investigation it was concluded that Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter, which won the £10,000 Caine prize, was ‘human-written’</p><p>The Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza has been cleared of using AI to write a prize-winning short story, after the prestigious Caine prize for African writers concluded that his entry was “human-written” after a month-long investigation.</p><p>Kundizeza’s story <a href="https://static1.squarespace.com/static/6a4f3fb6a6178e0225b39a4c/t/6a95fffc36f1fc568e02f7fe/1788215293124/3.The+Blue+Fighter.pdf">The Blue Fighter</a>, which charts the declining fortunes of a family after the father invests in fish tanks, was announced as the winner of the £10,000 prize on 6 October.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/books/2026/nov/12/zimbabwean-author-simbarashe-kundizeza-cleared-ai-caine-prize-winning-story">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/08/egypt-two-trains-deadly-collision</link>
      <description><p>President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo</p><p>Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said.</p><p>The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 50km (30 miles) south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/08/egypt-two-trains-deadly-collision">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/kenyan-doomsday-sect-leader-jailed-murders-paul-mackenzie</link>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/14/fires-heat-floods-extreme-weather-2026</link>
      <description><p>People around the world have contended with unprecedented weather events and their fatal effects caused by the climate catastrophe</p><p>After the world’s hottest summer since records began in 1850, the death toll from extreme weather in 2026 is already in the high tens of thousands. That is a conservative estimate and is certain to rise much higher.</p><p>As <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/cop31">Cop31</a> continues and scientists warn that <a href="https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/10/261027231200.htm">climate breakdown may be accelerating</a>, the Guardian looks back at a year of droughts, fires and floods as a reminder that, unless the world takes urgent action to cut emissions, this disastrous year will be one of the best of the rest of our lives.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/14/fires-heat-floods-extreme-weather-2026">Continue reading...</a></description>

    <item>
      <title>Storm Charles causes floods and flight cancellations across southern Europe</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/13/storm-charles-floods-flight-cancellations-southern-europe-weather</link>
      <description><p>Heavy rain and strong winds have also caused disruption across British Columbia, Canada, over the last week </p><p>Storm Charles has brought destructive weather to the Iberian peninsula this week, particularly in Portugal and the far south of Spain. Heavy rain and strong south-westerly winds arrived first in the Portuguese island of Madeira, before the system headed towards the mainland on 11 November. A wind gust of 84.5mph (136 km/h) was recorded at Funchal airport, alongside rainfall totals reaching 355mm (13.97in) in 12 hours. In Lisbon, 183 flights were cancelled on Wednesday, about a third of its normal daily traffic, while Madrid Barajas airport had 155 cancellations.</p><p>After causing widespread flooding in Spain and Portugal, the system moved on a north-easterly track through southern France and then towards northern Italy. This resulted in significant flooding in parts of Cannes, some of which caused rock falls and led to the closure of roads along the French Riviera. The Italian weather service issued a red rainfall warning, its highest level, for the area extending from Tuscany to Venezia. Further heavy rain is expected to fall in Italy and the Balkans over the next few days, with the latest forecast models indicating an additional 100mm could accumulate widely, while totals close to 200mm are likely in more mountainous areas.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/13/storm-charles-floods-flight-cancellations-southern-europe-weather">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Thursday briefing: What we do (and don’t) know about Alice Huang and the Nvidia affair</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/12/thursday-briefing-what-we-do-and-dont-know-about-alice-huang-and-the-nvidia-affair</link>
      <description><p>In today’s newsletter: US intelligence reportedly believes the former tech executive was recruited by Beijing, raising questions about the security of the AI industry and Trump’s close ties to Nvidia chief Jensen Huang</p><p></p><p>Good morning. Espionage is supposed to be a secretive business, and spies are supposed to be virtually invisible. That hasn’t been the case for Alice Huang, the mysterious Shanghai executive who formed a romantic relationship with Jensen Huang, the founder of Nvidia, one of America’s most powerful tech companies.</p><p>Many questions have arisen since it emerged that US intelligence believes that Huang (no relation of Jensen’s) is an asset recruited by the Chinese intelligence services to spy on behalf of Beijing. This morning’s newsletter explains what we know about the story, and what it tells us about the effectiveness of Chinese espionage. That’s after the headlines.</p><p><em><strong>UK </strong></em>| Ministers are considering <a       <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/14/activist-extradition-gaza-hamas-spanish-court</link>
      <description><p>James ‘Fergie’ Chambers, a Cox Enterprises heir, faced a two-hour hearing about alleged support for Hamas</p><p>A two-hour hearing in Spain’s high court Friday on the US extradition request of wealthy leftwing activist and philanthropist James “Fergie” Chambers turned out to be a study in contrasts.</p><p>Chambers’s defense took most of the session to query the US citizen and detail irregularities in the Trump administration’s extradition request – several of which the Guardian has <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/07/trump-administration-altered-translation-request-extradite-fergie-chambers">reported on</a> – as well as the figures of Spanish law that would lead the three-judge panel to deny the request; while the prosecutor sped through his case, head down, asking Chambers no questions at all.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/14/activist-extradition-gaza-hamas-spanish-court">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>UK-EU breakthrough will allow airport-style checks at Eurotunnel to avoid border ‘chaos’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/travel/2026/nov/14/eurotunnel-drive-in-fingerprint-trial-folkestone-calais-border</link>
      <description><p>Eurotunnel owner Getlink wants to replicate ‘airport experience’ at Folkestone and Calais, without making people get out of cars</p><p>Airport-style passport and fingerprinting controls are to be introduced at Eurotunnel in an attempt to prevent “short-term and long-term chaos” in Folkestone and Calais.</p><p>In a breakthrough for travellers, the European Commission has agreed to a new system in which an “eagle eye” camera system, already used in Rome and Paris airports to supervise fingerprinting and facial imaging, will be used at the border between the UK and France.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/travel/2026/nov/14/eurotunnel-drive-in-fingerprint-trial-folkestone-calais-border">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Prospect of partial return to Budapest by Central European University suggests confidence in Hungary’s future</p><p>A university that Viktor Orbán tried to chase out of Hungary is open to expanding its presence in Budapest, in a mark of confidence in the country’s democratic future.</p><p>Carsten Q Schneider, the interim president and rector of Central European University (CEU), said it was interested in increasing its programmes in Budapest, as long as this did not damage the student experience.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/14/university-hungary-orban-soros-ceu">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Hungary seizes $19.5m in cash found buried in forests amid graft inquiry</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/13/hungary-seizes-195m-in-cash-found-buried-in-forests-amid-graft-inquiry</link>
      <description><p>Anti-corruption agency carried out searches as part of investigation into Orbán-era minister accused of taking bribes</p><p>Hungary’s anti-corruption agency said on Friday it had seized cash worth $19.5m (£14.8m) buried in forests and hidden elsewhere while investigating an ex-minister of nationalist former leader Viktor Orbán’s cabinet.</p><p>Miklós Seszták, Hungary’s minister of national development between 2014 and 2018, is accused of taking bribes in a scheme involving the state transport company, purchasing secondhand buses at inflated prices.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/13/hungary-seizes-195m-in-cash-found-buried-in-forests-amid-graft-inquiry">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Kaja Kallas says Moscow is trying to divert attention from its aggression by raising issue of European security</p><p>The EU’s foreign policy chief has warned against “walking into the traps that Russia is setting” as she said Moscow was trying to start a debate about European security in order to divert attention from its aggression.</p><p>“We have one aggressor and one victim, and the aggressor does not have security concerns,” Kaja Kallas said on arrival at an EU leaders’ summit in Dublin. “Nobody has ever attacked them. The latest information, news and events in France, Europe and around the world.</description><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/</link><lastBuildDate>Sat, 14 Nov 2026 18:30:09 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>France</category><title>How France's student protests grew into a broader movement amid police violence</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261114-how-france-s-student-protests-grew-into-a-broader-movement-amid-police-violence</link><description>
What began in September as a student protest over deteriorating school conditions has over recent weeks grown into a broader social movement across France. The violent police response, notably against young protesters, has helped galvanise support, drawing in university students, trade unions and the wider public.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/7bafaefa-d940-11f1-a471-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T151110Z-1962061008-RC2PHOAWS3MA-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/7bafaefa-d940-11f1-a471-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T151110Z-1962061008-RC2PHOAWS3MA-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c5254f58-dea5-11f1-81d0-4703a0e08d35</guid><pubDate>Sat, 14 Nov 2026 11:11:37 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/7bafaefa-d940-11f1-a471-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T151110Z-1962061008-RC2PHOAWS3MA-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">© Abdul Saboor/Reuters</source><dc:creator>Sarah Elzas</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Fifth wave of French protests to focus on child protection and police laws</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261114-fifth-wave-of-french-protests-to-focus-on-child-protection-and-police-laws</link><description>
France faces more rallies on Saturday with demonstrators venting frustrations ranging from inflation, to child protection measures and opposition to a new police bill.  
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/3d7c7c2c-d93f-11f1-a046-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T145802Z-1961164086-RC2PHOAJPH70-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/3d7c7c2c-d93f-11f1-a046-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T145802Z-1961164086-RC2PHOAJPH70-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">628d1b7a-e010-11f1-9f24-738203d63293</guid><pubDate>Sat, 14 Nov 2026 11:03:51 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/3d7c7c2c-d93f-11f1-a046-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T145802Z-1961164086-RC2PHOAJPH70-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Abdul Saboor</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France marks 11th anniversary of Paris attacks with tribute at Stade de France</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261113-france-marks-11th-anniversary-of-paris-attacks-with-tribute-at-stade-de-france</link><description>
France is marking the 11th anniversary of the November 2015 Paris terrorist attacks on Friday, with commemorations honouring the 130 people killed. This year the Stade de France, one of the sites targeted by the attackers, hosts a sporting event on 13 November for the first time since the tragedy.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/f166e312-df75-11f1-adbe-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25317657554123.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/f166e312-df75-11f1-adbe-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25317657554123.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">a235f704-df5e-11f1-bb2c-85a37d07b862</guid><pubDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 15:08:48 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/f166e312-df75-11f1-adbe-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25317657554123.jpg">AP - Emma Da Silva</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France slams Russian ‘intimidation’ as fresh EU sanctions come into force</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261113-france-slams-russian-intimidation-fedorova-as-fresh-eu-sanctions-come-into-force</link><description>
The European Union will approve more ​sanctions against Russia on Monday, the bulk of which were proposed by France, the country's Minister for European Affairs Benjamin Haddad said on Thursday. He also warned that Paris would not be intimidated by Moscow’s decision to ban two French journalists and two MPs from entering the country.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c0a81bba-5f78-11f1-b8ae-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/photo-2026-06-03-19-52-33.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c0a81bba-5f78-11f1-b8ae-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/photo-2026-06-03-19-52-33.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">9187c500-de81-11f1-bc9f-6b48e96878ad</guid><pubDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:44:47 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c0a81bba-5f78-11f1-b8ae-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/photo-2026-06-03-19-52-33.jpg">© RFI</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France requests arrest warrants for Iranian suspects over supermarket cyberattack</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261111-france-requests-arrest-warrants-for-iranian-suspects-over-supermarket-cyberattack</link><description>
France has requested international arrest warrants for three Iranian men over October’s cyberattack on supermarket fridges, while Tehran rejects the allegations as “baseless and malicious”. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a5408b50-dcf0-11f1-b997-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-29T100226Z-1803060916-RC2Q1OAGCX8L-RTRMADP-3-USA-MILITARY-FREEZERS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a5408b50-dcf0-11f1-b997-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-29T100226Z-1803060916-RC2Q1OAGCX8L-RTRMADP-3-USA-MILITARY-FREEZERS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">8a8f8ab4-ddcb-11f1-8b47-cfca036f86fe</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 16:00:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a5408b50-dcf0-11f1-b997-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-29T100226Z-1803060916-RC2Q1OAGCX8L-RTRMADP-3-USA-MILITARY-FREEZERS.jpg">© Stephane Mahe/Reuters</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Zemmour joins 2027 French presidential race vowing to expel unemployed foreigners</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261111-zemmour-joins-2027-race-vowing-to-expel-jobless-foreigners</link><description>
Far-right politician Eric Zemmour has formally entered next year’s French presidential race. He is promising a sharp cut in immigration, and the expulsion of foreigners who are out of work, even if they live in France legally.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/75824288-ddc6-11f1-b11b-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-c87e2bl.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/75824288-ddc6-11f1-b11b-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-c87e2bl.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">e4ed6918-ddc6-11f1-ab44-f53e2031ebff</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 12:55:43 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/75824288-ddc6-11f1-b11b-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-c87e2bl.jpg">© SIMON WOHLFAHRT / AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Emmanuel and Brigitte Macron file new lawsuit in US against right-wing influencer</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261111-emmanuel-and-brigitte-macron-file-new-lawsuit-in-us-against-right-wing-influencer</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron and his wife Brigitte have filed a new defamation lawsuit in the United States against conservative influencer Candace Owens, who claims the French First Lady is a transgender woman.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c32c0b32-dcf8-11f1-9d6d-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26281300022948.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c32c0b32-dcf8-11f1-9d6d-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26281300022948.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">e1014d56-dcf9-11f1-b466-e9d2e52e2a56</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:59:26 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c32c0b32-dcf8-11f1-9d6d-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26281300022948.jpg">© Abdul Saboor/Reuters pool via AP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Teachers divided over compulsory 11 November ceremonies at schools</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261111-teachers-divided-over-compulsory-11-november-ceremonies-at-schools</link><description>
A new government initiative requires primary schools across France to hold ceremonies honouring those who died for the country. But teachers are divided over its purpose and the role of the military in education. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12bc0fa4-1086-11ea-8502-005056a99247/w:1024/p:16x9/2012-11-11T144200Z_94089871_GM1E8BB1QZK01_RTRMADP_3_FRANCE.JPG"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12bc0fa4-1086-11ea-8502-005056a99247/w:1024/p:16x9/2012-11-11T144200Z_94089871_GM1E8BB1QZK01_RTRMADP_3_FRANCE.JPG" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">8f4305e2-dd0b-11f1-ad88-012109f6bc5c</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 06:05:01 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12bc0fa4-1086-11ea-8502-005056a99247/w:1024/p:16x9/2012-11-11T144200Z_94089871_GM1E8BB1QZK01_RTRMADP_3_FRANCE.JPG">REUTERS/Pascal Rosssignol</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French students demonstrate solidarity in the fight for better schools</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261110-french-students-demonstrate-solidarity-in-the-fight-for-better-schools</link><description>
It began as a protest over crumbling classrooms and missing teachers, but France's student movement is now challenging the political establishment to give young people more of a say in decisions about their future. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/37f55a2a-d6b6-11f1-94f8-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26306393160391.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/37f55a2a-d6b6-11f1-94f8-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26306393160391.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f19af422-dc5f-11f1-a6cf-03231484c166</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 21:55:52 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/37f55a2a-d6b6-11f1-94f8-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26306393160391.jpg">AP Photo/Nicolas Garriga - Nicolas Garriga</source><dc:creator>Alison Hird</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French student protests continue amid deadlock over education reforms</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261110-french-student-protests-continue-amid-deadlock-over-education-reforms</link><description>
Students and teachers are planning a new day of strikes and demonstrations on Tuesday, as talks with the government remain deadlocked, nearly two months after the start of protests by high school and university students.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/29cb24b4-c8b7-11f1-9aa3-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-15T145022Z-1497667603-RC2N3OANCMHS-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/29cb24b4-c8b7-11f1-9aa3-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-15T145022Z-1497667603-RC2N3OANCMHS-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">37288fa8-dcd4-11f1-aace-7ff548d44c0a</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 06:59:03 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/29cb24b4-c8b7-11f1-9aa3-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-15T145022Z-1497667603-RC2N3OANCMHS-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">© Stephane Mahe/Reuters</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner joins race for French presidency</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-olympic-judo-champion-teddy-riner-joins-race-for-french-presidency</link><description>
France's five-time Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner announced on Monday that he would run in next year's presidential election, expressing concern particularly over "the rise of the far right".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/24e10c34-dc35-11f1-9eaf-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26313423095961.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/24e10c34-dc35-11f1-9eaf-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26313423095961.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ff9ac7be-dc3c-11f1-a6ee-d528d7ed3f40</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 17:44:42 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/24e10c34-dc35-11f1-9eaf-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26313423095961.jpg">© AP - Michel Euler</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French PM's move to increase minimum wage fails to convince unions</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-french-pm-s-move-to-increase-minimum-wage-fails-to-convince-unions</link><description>
The French government on Monday announced a 1.6 percent increase in the national minimum wage, alongside a series of measures aimed at easing cost of living pressures. However, the decision fell well short of the demands of trade unions, who have called for fresh protests in the coming days.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/391ca27a-db78-11f1-86b0-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26311499885536.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/391ca27a-db78-11f1-86b0-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26311499885536.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1fb23d3e-dc42-11f1-9f6d-714e057b766f</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 17:36:17 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/391ca27a-db78-11f1-86b0-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26311499885536.jpg">© Emma Da Silva/AP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'I still have nightmares': victim of police violence seeks justice six years on</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-i-still-have-nightmares-victim-of-police-violence-seeks-justice-six-years-on-michel-zecler</link><description>
Three French police officers are due to go on trial on Monday over the brutal beating of black music producer Michel Zecler in Paris in 2020 – a case that sparked nationwide outrage over police violence and racism.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/88ce45b6-dba1-11f1-91d2-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/FRANCE-JUSTICE-MICHEL-ZECLER.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/88ce45b6-dba1-11f1-91d2-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/FRANCE-JUSTICE-MICHEL-ZECLER.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0aa97116-dc27-11f1-890c-17b2c492ee48</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 14:29:18 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/88ce45b6-dba1-11f1-91d2-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/FRANCE-JUSTICE-MICHEL-ZECLER.jpg">AFP - JOEL SAGET</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Mélenchon bets on radical change as French presidential race takes shape</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-m%C3%A9lenchon-bets-on-radical-change-as-french-presidential-race-takes-shape</link><description>
Leader of the hard-left France Unbowed party Jean-Luc Mélenchon has vowed to pursue an uncompromising programme of radical change, as he bids for the French presidency in 2027 – despite warnings that his divisive politics could ultimately hand victory to far-right National Rally leader Marine Le Pen.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/28b90688-dc1f-11f1-84be-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/M%C3%A9lenchon-7-November-2026.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/28b90688-dc1f-11f1-84be-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/M%C3%A9lenchon-7-November-2026.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">273d195c-dc1a-11f1-8d60-5f29074843e0</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 13:01:32 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/28b90688-dc1f-11f1-84be-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/M%C3%A9lenchon-7-November-2026.jpg">©  KENZO TRIBOUILLARD / AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French food bank donations fall as frequency of use spikes in cost of living crisis</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-drop-in-french-food-bank-collection-as-rising-cost-of-living-hits-donations</link><description>
France’s annual food bank collection has gathered less than expected in the face of the rising cost of living, which has left people with less to spend on donations. The three-day campaign, which ended on Sunday, aimed to collect enough food to provide the equivalent of 20 million meals.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b1392996-dbc2-11f1-af3e-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32TL9GD-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b1392996-dbc2-11f1-af3e-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32TL9GD-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b7b3dffa-dc2b-11f1-8a7f-0f7ff0c2412a</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 12:09:22 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b1392996-dbc2-11f1-af3e-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32TL9GD-1.jpg">© Mehdi Fedouach/AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French MPs weigh up debate on right-wing TV channel ban as petition tops 1m</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-french-mps-to-weigh-debate-on-banning-conservative-tv-channel-as-petition-tops-1m-cnews</link><description>
A petition calling for French television channel CNews, often compared to American broadcaster Fox News, to be shut down has received more than a million signatures, two days before lawmakers meet to consider whether a ban should be debated in parliament.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b0dc3b9c-dba8-11f1-b566-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D66Z6FA.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b0dc3b9c-dba8-11f1-b566-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D66Z6FA.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">19210fc8-dc0a-11f1-bd4e-25468b64d7d5</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 06:52:14 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b0dc3b9c-dba8-11f1-b566-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D66Z6FA.jpg">© Anne-Christine Poujoulat/AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Unions vow to maintain pressure on government after fourth wave of protests</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261108-unions-vow-to-keep-pressure-on-french-government-after-fourth-wave-of-protests</link><description>
Education union chiefs on Sunday vowed to maintain pressure on the French government after student organisations called for another day of nationwide strikes and demonstrations on Tuesday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a57fc52e-db63-11f1-b306-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/prote.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a57fc52e-db63-11f1-b306-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/prote.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">36cb7bb6-dac6-11f1-b148-e9346ba72bac</guid><pubDate>Sun, 08 Nov 2026 11:00:57 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a57fc52e-db63-11f1-b306-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/prote.jpg">AP Photo/Emma Da Silva - Emma Da Silva</source><dc:creator>Paul Myers</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>French students vow to continue protests</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/video/20261107-french-students-vow-to-continue-protests-paris</link><description>
French pupils and students are protesting and blockading schools over poor conditions and a university admissions system (Parcoursup) seen as over-selective and opaque. Despite recent concessions by the government, students at Hélène Boucher high school in Paris say they'll continue, even after riot place were sent to break their blockade.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bed31678-c945-11f1-84f0-638c1c1f5fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-16T075646Z-1864054812-RC274OA7GQ58-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST-2.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bed31678-c945-11f1-84f0-638c1c1f5fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-16T075646Z-1864054812-RC274OA7GQ58-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST-2.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">8c9b5ff0-dab9-11f1-a45a-31b57fcb4ae5</guid><pubDate>Sat, 07 Nov 2026 15:02:47 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France braces for second day of protests within 48 hours</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261107-france-braces-for-second-day-of-protests-within-48-hours</link><description>
Hundreds of thousands of people were expected to take to the streets on Saturday for a day of protests over the poor conditions in schools and the rising cost of living.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb2ec67e-d9cd-11f1-a5cc-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T151241Z-1266580735-RC2OHOAVSIEZ-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb2ec67e-d9cd-11f1-a5cc-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T151241Z-1266580735-RC2OHOAVSIEZ-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">33ad1cbc-da96-11f1-8df4-1da1eb33321e</guid><pubDate>Sat, 07 Nov 2026 12:10:04 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb2ec67e-d9cd-11f1-a5cc-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T151241Z-1266580735-RC2OHOAVSIEZ-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Hannah McKay</source><dc:creator>Paul Myers</dc:creator></item><item><category>Spotlight on France</category><title>Podcast: France's student protests and how they fuelled a larger social movement</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/podcasts/spotlight-on-france/20261106-podcast-france-s-student-protests-and-how-they-fuelled-a-larger-social-movement-may-68</link><description>
A look at France's high school protests and how they have fed into an ongoing social movement. What are the students protesting against? What impact has the police crackdown had? How has the government reacted? And a comparison with student movements of the past.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/884fdc42-d9cd-11f1-80bf-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/episode-spotlight-on-france-episode-152-peach-pink.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/884fdc42-d9cd-11f1-80bf-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/episode-spotlight-on-france-episode-152-peach-pink.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">bcd965aa-d9cd-11f1-b272-af07f9a85ea6</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 15:29:10 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Sarah Elzas</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French lawyers to sue interior minister over 'mutilation' of young protesters</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261106-french-lawyers-to-sue-interior-minister-over-mutilation-of-young-protesters</link><description>
Lawyers representing at least 18 people injured during protests in France in recent weeks say they intend to file a complaint against Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez over his alleged responsibility for police brutality.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ad744280-bea5-11f1-8056-578a4b968fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-02T104258Z-1424347954-RC2XUNAITHZX-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ad744280-bea5-11f1-8056-578a4b968fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-02T104258Z-1424347954-RC2XUNAITHZX-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">dba18ef0-d9e5-11f1-863b-f351e1b5079d</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 14:39:42 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ad744280-bea5-11f1-8056-578a4b968fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-02T104258Z-1424347954-RC2XUNAITHZX-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Nacho Doce</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'AI cannot do everything': bullying experts warn against confiding in chatbots</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261106-one-quarter-of-young-bullying-victims-turning-to-ai-for-help-study-finds</link><description>
As a growing number of victims turn to artificial intelligence for help, experts warn that, while a virtual confidante can offer temporary relief, the focus must be on prevention and support.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/808c3c9c-cd36-11f1-b7ef-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/yamu-jay-school-bullying-9060270.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/808c3c9c-cd36-11f1-b7ef-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/yamu-jay-school-bullying-9060270.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">71185a8c-d797-11f1-a35f-45b5729425b2</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 09:35:34 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/808c3c9c-cd36-11f1-b7ef-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/yamu-jay-school-bullying-9060270.jpg">© pixabay / Yamu_Jay</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Latest figures show domestic violence still major problem in France</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261106-chilling-figures-show-domestic-violence-still-major-problem-in-france</link><description>
French authorities recorded 285,000 victims of domestic violence in 2025, mostly women, representing a 5 percent increase in a year. It comes as lawmakers debate a new law against sexual and gender-based violence that is due to be finalised at the beginning of 2027.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb36a16c-43a7-11f1-8f1d-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26090564561960.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb36a16c-43a7-11f1-8f1d-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26090564561960.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">77dc943a-d92e-11f1-90a5-5193511bd582</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 06:08:15 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb36a16c-43a7-11f1-8f1d-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26090564561960.jpg">© Andreea Alexandru / AP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>‘We’ll get them’: Macron’s private comments on rivals revealed in new book</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261105-we-ll-get-them-macron-s-private-comments-on-rivals-revealed-in-new-book</link><description>
Private messages exchanged between French President Emmanuel Macron and journalist Françoise Degois over two years have been published in a new book, revealing his views on political rivals, the rise of the far right and his own leadership. The president reportedly learnt of the book’s existence just three days before its release.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb95d9d2-d896-11f1-b8ef-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP22177506677032-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb95d9d2-d896-11f1-b8ef-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP22177506677032-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ed7d8d46-d8f9-11f1-8648-c35846abfa7a</guid><pubDate>Thu, 05 Nov 2026 16:07:25 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb95d9d2-d896-11f1-b8ef-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP22177506677032-1.jpg">© AP - Susan Walsh </source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French prosecutors investigate €100m cyberattack on Crédit Mutuel banking group</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261105-french-prosecutors-investigate-%E2%82%AC100m-cyberattack-on-cr%C3%A9dit-mutuel-banking-group</link><description>
French prosecutors have opened an investigation into a sophisticated cyberattack on Crédit Mutuel Arkéa involving fraudulent transfers estimated at around €100 million, as the Brittany-based banking group races to recover the stolen funds.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a8dda14a-d907-11f1-a6f6-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/Cr%C3%A9dit-Mutuel-Ark%C3%A9a.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a8dda14a-d907-11f1-a6f6-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/Cr%C3%A9dit-Mutuel-Ark%C3%A9a.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">d4c86e50-d8f5-11f1-8292-031c66ea2070</guid><pubDate>Thu, 05 Nov 2026 12:31:26 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a8dda14a-d907-11f1-a6f6-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/Cr%C3%A9dit-Mutuel-Ark%C3%A9a.jpg">AFP - FRED TANNEAU</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

      <description><p>‘We have further to go,’ says Huw Pill after increase to 4% this month as Bank seeks to tackle rising inflation</p><p>The Bank of England will probably need to raise interest rates next month and again in early 2027 to combat rising inflation, its chief economist has said.</p><p>Signalling a sharp rise in mortgage payments for an estimated <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/money/2026/nov/02/mortgage-payments-rise-2027-interest-rates">2.3 million homeowners</a> who will have to refinance their loans next year, Huw Pill said that while the decision to nudge interest rates from 3.75% to 4% earlier this month was a “significant step” towards getting monetary policy into a better place, “we ⁠have further to go”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/14/interest-rate-rises-inflation-bank-of-england-chief-economist">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Thousands of flights still canceled as officials blamed ageing air control system for nationwide grounding</p><p>The Trump administration says Friday’s four-hour nationwide Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/13/faa-ground-stop-flights-explained">ground stop</a> that delayed or canceled thousands of flight stemmed from routine maintenance.</p><p>At a news briefing on Saturday, the US transportation secretary, Sean Duffy, said that the issues began when a contractor was performing “routine maintenance” at a remote FAA facility to “switch telecommunications lines” from copper wire to fiber optic cable.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/14/faa-ground-stop-flights-resume-airport-chaos">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>‘The social contract is broken’: young people on feeling shut out of careers</title>

      <description><p>In the first instalment of a new series, four young people reveal the impact of an endless cycle of applications and rejections</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/14/guardian-young-people-search-for-work">Guardian to follow lives of eight young people in their search for jobs</a></p></li></ul><p></p><p>“I’ve been demoralised by the process, just constantly applying, then interviewing.       <description><p>The environmental and economic dilemmas he faces are formidable but, with a bold plan, he could set an example for leaders around the world</p><p>For politicians of the centre-left especially, it’s the great dilemma of the age. How do you do what everyone can see is essential to save the planet from boiling – even as your voters demand action to get the economy growing and to make life more affordable? Plenty of activists will tell you there’s no contradiction, that tackling the climate crisis makes economic as well as ecological sense and, in the long term, you know they’re right. But you don’t live in the long term. You’re running the government right now and facing several unavoidable, binary choices.</p><p>Andy Burnham is a prime example. This week, <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/11/uk-appoints-worlds-first-special-representative-for-climate-security">he addressed the Cop summit in Antalya</a>, promising “a new era of British leadership” in the struggle against global heating. It’s important to him to talk that way: his political strategy relies on shrinking the appeal of the Green party, whose electoral success earlier this year helped remove his predecessor. But talk only takes you so far. Eventually the words have to be matched by action.</p><p>Jonathan Freedland is a Guardian columnist</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/nov/13/fight-climate-crisis-growth-andy-burnham-economic-leaders">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Chief financial officer, reportedly disparaged by Huang during summer meeting, to take over on short-term basis</p><p>The hunt is on for a new Nvidia CEO.       <title>The folly of just-in-time supply chains | Letters</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026/nov/13/the-folly-of-just-in-time-supply-chains</link>
      <description><p><strong>Hannah Walker </strong>says systems designed to minimise expenditure in the name of efficiency can end up less capable of fulfilling their actual purpose</p><p>The article by Steven Strogatz and&nbsp;Alex Townsend on the dangers&nbsp;of excessive optimisation identifies a problem extending far&nbsp;beyond mathematics and artificial intelligence (<a href="https://www.theguardian.com/books/2026/nov/08/the-efficiency-trap-why-optimising-everything-can-backfire-badly">The efficiency trap: why optimising everything can backfire, badly, 8 November</a>).</p><p>The widespread adoption of just-in-time supply chains illustrates it perfectly. By eliminating inventories and spare capacity, businesses reduced costs and improved efficiency, but frequently transferred those savings into risks that remained invisible until something went wrong. The&nbsp;disruption of global manufacturing during the pandemic exposed the&nbsp;consequences.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026/nov/13/the-folly-of-just-in-time-supply-chains">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Five-year project will create wildlife corridors by building wetlands and increase access to green and blue spaces</p><p>Bristol could become home to the UK’s first “wetland city” thanks to a charity’s efforts to create vast wildlife corridors that will reduce flood risk and give people more access to green and blue spaces.</p><p>The Wildfowl &amp; Wetlands Trust (WWT) said the five-year initiative would include more than 200 projects to restore and create wetlands across the city.       <description><p>Eccentric and overhyped, Tesla’s Cybertruck became a stand-in for Elon Musk during his ascent in the Republican party. It will join the ranks of other vehicles symbolic of their eras – for better or for worse</p><p>Three days after a historic blue tsunami changed America’s political landscape, Elon Musk announced Tesla would end production of its hulking Cybertruck next year.</p><p>Was it a coincidence? Maybe. Musk said the move was “to make room for increased Cybercab production”, referring to Tesla’s Robotaxi. But the combined circumstances felt highly appropriate: it was the end of an era.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/ng-interactive/2026/nov/13/cybertruck-maga-hat-on-wheels-end">Continue reading...</a></description>

    <item>
      <title>Here Manchester United go again, taking the Two Ronnies route to hiring a new boss | Jonathan Wilson</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/14/here-manchester-united-go-again-taking-the-two-ronnies-route-to-hiring-a-new-boss</link>
      <description><p>Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival feels like yet another appointment that would have been better made a few years ago</p><p>Magnusson: And your time starts ... now! What is paleontology? Smithers: Yes, absolutely correct. Magnusson: What’s the name of the directory that lists members of the peerage? Smithers: A study of old fossils. Magnusson: Correct. Who are Len Murray and Sir Geoffrey Howe? Smithers: Burke’s. Magnusson: Correct. What is the difference between a donkey and an ass? Smithers: One’s a trade union leader, the other’s a member of the Cabinet …</p><p>One of the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/media/2016/mar/31/ronnie-corbett-best-clips-two-ronnies-fork-handles-extras">Two Ronnies’</a> most celebrated sketches involves a Mastermind contestant whose specialist subject is answering the previous question. History repeats itself: the first time as comedy, the second time as Manchester United, who seem continually to be answering not the question of who would be the best available manager now, but who might have been the best available manager a few years ago.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/14/here-manchester-united-go-again-taking-the-two-ronnies-route-to-hiring-a-new-boss">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>De la Fuente adamant there is no racism in Spain despite England reminder to players</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/14/luis-de-la-fuente-spain-england-racism-thomas-tuchel-natiions-league</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>De la Fuente tells Tuchel ‘we’re not racists, none of us’</p></li><li><p>Tuchel hits out at media for ‘creating confusion’</p></li></ul><p>Luis de la Fuente has told Thomas Tuchel there is no racism in Spain after the England coach’s admission that he would remind his players of the anti-racism protocol prior to their meeting at the Metropolitano on Sunday night.</p><p>This will be the first time the countries play each other in Madrid since some of England’s black players were subjected to racist abuse <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2004/dec/21/newsstory.sport12">in a match at the Santiago Bernabéu in 2004</a>. And although England have returned to Spain three times without incident since then, twice in Seville and once in Alicante, Tuchel <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/13/thotmas-tuchel-england-anti-racism-protocols-spain-nations-league">was asked on Friday about going back</a> in the buildup to Sunday’s game. The England coach replied that England “will not expect anything [untoward]” but also said: “Maybe we take our five minutes to inform the players about the protocol if there is a precedent [in Madrid].”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/14/luis-de-la-fuente-spain-england-racism-thomas-tuchel-natiions-league">Continue reading...</a></description>

    <item>
      <title>The beautiful game: revived art prize gives football its creative due once more | Emma John</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/13/football-association-art-prize</link>
      <description><p>Football and the art world have long remained distant but the breadth of entries for this year’s award reveals a healthy revival</p><p>It may be the Beautiful Game, but in its early decades football was a rare subject for artists. The Italian Futurist Umberto Boccioni whirled an athlete’s body into a vortex of movement in his 1913 painting Dynamism of a Soccer Player<em>.</em> You can see one of the earliest fine art depictions of a match – a smoggy, factory-adjactent scene called Any Wintry Afternoon in England <em>– </em>at the Manchester Art Gallery. If 1930s abstraction is more your thing, you can enjoy decoding the geometric shapes in Kazimir Malevich’s Painterly Realism of a Football Player – Color Masses in the 4th Dimension. I’m guessing the small green pea shape is a ball.</p><p>These, in any case, were exceptions. In 1953 the Football Assocition launched an art prize, backed by the newly formed Arts Council: the winning works included Going To The Match by LS Lowry, with its crowds flocking to Bolton Wanderers’ then home ground, Burnden Park. An exhibition of the submissions, Football and The Fine Arts, toured the country and the Football Association secretary, Sir Stanley Rous, said he hoped it would finally break the barrier between those two worlds.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/13/football-association-art-prize">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Clara Luvanga strikes as Washington Spirit beat Utah to reach third straight NWSL final</title>

      <description><ul><li><p>Tanzanian scores second-half winner in 2-1 victory</p></li><li><p>Spirit reach fifth NWSL final and third in succession</p></li><li><p>Washington will chase second title at home ground</p></li></ul><p>Clara Luvanga scored her second goal of the postseason in the 57th minute, capitalizing on an errant pass as the Washington Spirit reached their fifth NWSL Championship and third straight with a 2-1 semi-final victory over the Utah Royals on Saturday.</p><p>Luvanga raced on to Nuria Rábano’s ill-advised ball after it rolled past Utah center-back Tatumn Milazzo, then chipped it delicately over the advancing goalkeeper Mandy McGlynn for the winner.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/14/washington-spirit-utah-royals-nwsl-semi-final-clara-luvanga">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>‘Pregnancy does not mean game over’: meet the footballers challenging the myths | Moving the Goalposts</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/12/pregnancy-womens-football-moving-the-goalposts-newsletter</link>
      <description><p>Claire Emslie and Emma Kelly are among those taking advantage of new research and guidelines for pregnant players</p><p>Claire Emslie wasn’t expecting to be able to <a href="https://www.instagram.com/p/DRVlP5iEgRR/?img_index=2">run at 81% of her max speed</a> at 32 weeks pregnant.</p><p>Emslie, a Scotland international who also plays as a forward for <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/angel-city-fc">Angel City FC</a>, documented her journey through pregnancy and football training on social media and is part of a growing number of professional female footballers who are getting pregnant in their athletic prime and approaching motherhood with a fresh mindset. Rather than marking the end of a career (notably, <a href="https://www.mirror.co.uk/3am/celebrity-news/lioness-millie-bright-pregnant-first-37623021">Millie Bright announced her pregnancy</a> in September, months after having retired), pregnancy can mark both a continuation and a renewal.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/12/pregnancy-womens-football-moving-the-goalposts-newsletter">Continue reading...</a></description>

L'Afrique peut-elle former ses propres élites sans les envoyer étudier à l'étranger ? Au Maroc, l'Université Mohammed VI Polytechnique (UM6P) s'impose parmi les établissements africains les mieux classés à l'international. Recherche, intelligence artificielle, robotique, agriculture : l'université mise sur des formations de pointe pour répondre aux défis du continent. Mais cette excellence est-elle accessible à tous ? Et ce modèle peut-il être reproduit ailleurs en Afrique ? Sa Benjamin Traoré, professeur de droit public et directeur du programme Droit et Gouvernance à l'UM6P, est l'invité de Fatimata Wane dans le Journal de l'Afrique sur France 24.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/33ef4b46-e077-11f1-a070-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261114-215038-215826-CS-01.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/33ef4b46-e077-11f1-a070-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261114-215038-215826-CS-01.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">3a23c488-e077-11f1-9d80-319ec9b15393</guid><pubDate>Sat, 14 Nov 2026 22:24:21 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Journal de l'Afrique</category><title>Présidence de la Francophonie : Louise Mushikiwabo "candidate jusqu'au bout"</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/journal-de-l-afrique/20261114-pr%C3%A9sidence-de-la-francophonie-louise-mushikiwabo-candidate-jusqu-au-bout</link><description>

Les pays membres sont en ce moment réunis au Cambodge et doivent choisir qui sera à la tête de l’OIF.  Et cela a bien évidemment fait réagir sur le continent…
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/5c4068b4-e077-11f1-9670-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/FRDN-JOURNAL-AFRIQUE-261114-2027-Ep-75.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/5c4068b4-e077-11f1-9670-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/FRDN-JOURNAL-AFRIQUE-261114-2027-Ep-75.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">887cc624-e078-11f1-b0f1-e36b04d82a3f</guid><pubDate>Sat, 14 Nov 2026 22:12:50 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Fatimata WANE</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Acte V du mouvement social : des revendications variées, une affluence en baisse</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261114-acte-v-du-mouvement-social-des-revendications-vari%C3%A9es-une-affluence-en-baisse</link><description>
Lors de l'acte V du mouvement social qui ébranle la France, quelque 106 000 à 200 000 personnes ont défilé samedi dans toute la France, selon les chiffres du ministère de l'Intérieur et l'intersyndicale jeune (Union étudiante, USL, Fage, Unef). Quelques incidents se sont produits et des journalistes ont été agressés.

Le producteur de musique avait été violemment interpellé en 2020 et affirme conserver d'importantes séquelles physiques et psychologiques. Les fonctionnaires mis en cause encourent jusqu'à quinze ans de prison et 15 000 euros d'amende. Reportage France 2.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8795315c-e036-11f1-a108-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261114-141057-141250-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8795315c-e036-11f1-a108-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261114-141057-141250-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">8c87bcf2-e036-11f1-8015-4155d6e70041</guid><pubDate>Sat, 14 Nov 2026 14:47:17 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Asie-Pacifique</category><title>Sommet de la francophonie : pour contrer le Rwanda, la RDC favorable au candidat roumain</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/asie-pacifique/20261114-sommet-francophonie-contrer-rwanda-rdc-favorable-au-candidat-roumain</link><description>
Alors que les 53 dirigeants de l'Organisation internationale de la francophonie sont réunis à Phnom Penh du 14 au 16 novembre pour désigner le nouveau secrétaire général, le sommet est miné par des tensions entre la République démocratique du Congo et le Rwanda. Kinshasa est prête à soutenir le candidat roumain pour s'opposer à la réélection de la Rwandaise Louise Mushikiwabo, en poste depuis 2018. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/78e68f44-e035-11f1-8f9a-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-13T032859Z-935596881-RC2OMOAE8G9E-RTRMADP-3-CAMBODIA-FRANCOPHONIE.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/78e68f44-e035-11f1-8f9a-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-13T032859Z-935596881-RC2OMOAE8G9E-RTRMADP-3-CAMBODIA-FRANCOPHONIE.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">e50e972a-e035-11f1-947e-3174bed47283</guid><pubDate>Sat, 14 Nov 2026 14:34:30 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/78e68f44-e035-11f1-8f9a-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-13T032859Z-935596881-RC2OMOAE8G9E-RTRMADP-3-CAMBODIA-FRANCOPHONIE.jpg">© Soveit Yarn, Reuters</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Au Sri Lanka, le jardin de Kandy, écrin tropical parmi les plus beaux d'Asie</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261114-au-sri-lanka-le-jardin-de-kandy-%C3%A9crin-tropical-parmi-les-plus-beaux-d-asie</link><description>
À Kandy, au Sri Lanka, ce jardin botanique réputé pour être l'un des plus beaux d'Asie abrite de nombreuses espèces tropicales protégées. Chaque année, il attire des centaines de milliers de visiteurs venus découvrir sa végétation exceptionnelle. Reportage de C. Devagenère et L. Delfolie (France 2).
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a6bfdd0-e02e-11f1-9a40-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261114-133933-134245-CS-01.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a6bfdd0-e02e-11f1-9a40-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261114-133933-134245-CS-01.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0f7c13d2-e02e-11f1-9e84-f356f2ab11be</guid><pubDate>Sat, 14 Nov 2026 13:50:39 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Éco/Tech</category><title>L'affaire Nvidia s'invite dans les discussions sur la sécurité de l'IA entre la Chine et les États-Unis</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9co-tech/20261114-affaire-nvidia-invite-dans-discussions-s%C3%A9curit%C3%A9-ia-entre-chine-%C3%A9tats-unis</link><description>
Le président américain Donald Trump et son homologue chinois Xi Jinping tenteront la semaine prochaine de dépasser l'affaire Nvidia pour trouver un terrain d'entente sur la sécurité en matière d'IA, lors du sommet de la Coopération économique Asie-Pacifique (Apec), alors que les craintes enflent quant aux risques liés à l'IA.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2b26f062-e01e-11f1-a680-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26281674389128.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2b26f062-e01e-11f1-a680-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26281674389128.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0488eea0-e01f-11f1-a42d-f5703b2f4074</guid><pubDate>Sat, 14 Nov 2026 13:18:56 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2b26f062-e01e-11f1-a680-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26281674389128.jpg">© Julia Demaree Nikhinson, AP Photo</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Café des sports</category><title>Équipe de France : premier couac pour Zidane !</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/caf%C3%A9-des-sports/20261114-%C3%A9quipe-france-premier-couac-pour-zidane</link><description>
La France s'est inclinée face à l'Italie (3-1) en Ligue des nations, jeudi soir. C'est la première défaite de Zinedine Zidane à la tête des Bleus. Un équilibre est-il à retrouver ? L’absence de Mbappé a-t-elle pesé ? Les Bleus devront s'imposer dimanche s'ils veulent se qualifier pour les quarts de finale.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a9b7d1ba-e02a-11f1-b111-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-355be4e9.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a9b7d1ba-e02a-11f1-b111-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-355be4e9.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">95b0343a-df6e-11f1-9710-07459da6ff6e</guid><pubDate>Sat, 14 Nov 2026 12:59:13 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Annie GASNIER</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>"Je ne pensais quand même pas avoir un père nazi" : Edith Pagot, née dans un Lebensborn</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261114-lebensborn-pouponniere-nazie-allemagne-enfants-seconde-guerre-mondiale-edith</link><description>
Il y a 80 ans, en 1946, deux convois d'enfants, dont certains nés dans un Lebensborn, une pouponnière nazie, étaient accueillis à Commercy, dans la Meuse, en provenance d'Allemagne. Parmi eux se trouvait Edith Pagot. Jusqu'à aujourd'hui, cette femme adoptée ignorait qu'elle était née dans un Lebensborn. Elle ne l'a appris que cette année, après des recherches entreprises par sa fille.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9490f12c-c0c2-11f1-985b-69fad0a7cb9f/w:1024/p:16x9/main-lebensborn.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9490f12c-c0c2-11f1-985b-69fad0a7cb9f/w:1024/p:16x9/main-lebensborn.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">8761c200-c0c3-11f1-8ef6-f76e46373e98</guid><pubDate>Sat, 14 Nov 2026 12:57:53 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9490f12c-c0c2-11f1-985b-69fad0a7cb9f/w:1024/p:16x9/main-lebensborn.png">© Studio graphique FMM</source><dc:creator>Stéphanie TROUILLARD</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

While the extension of France’s health pass and other new anti-Covid 19 measures announced by President Emmanuel Macron Monday night are yet to be hammered out in detail, what’s certain is that a full-throttled return to a normal life of frequenting café terraces, restaurants, cinemas, theatres and other culture and leisure activities will now hinge on having a pass sanitaire (or health pass).

French President Emmanuel Macron and his wife Brigitte filed a second lawsuit against US right-wing podcaster Candace Owens over false claims on her gender, accusing her of continuing to spread the allegations and profiting from them despite earlier legal action.

Christian Boltanski, one of France's top contemporary artists whose multimedia works probed the meaning of mortality and memory, has died aged 76, a former museum director told AFP on Sunday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b7135ce8-e4c8-11eb-89be-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Wed, 14 Jul 2021 18:44:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg">© Miguel Riopa, AFP</source><dc:creator>NEWS WIRES</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'Crumbs': French PM's 1.6% minimum wage increase fails to placate unions</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261109-french-pm-lecornu-announces-increase-minimum-wage-bid-to-calm-protests</link><description>
French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced on Monday that a planned 1.6% increase in the minimum wage would be brought forward from January to December after holding talks with trade unions and business leaders over the cost-of-living crisis that has fuelled weeks of unrest across France. The increase fell well short of the demands of unions, which have called for fresh protests in the coming days.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23136886-dc33-11f1-b2ff-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6WB27W.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23136886-dc33-11f1-b2ff-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6WB27W.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f6ee1d4e-dc43-11f1-9280-633626f68692</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 13:52:34 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23136886-dc33-11f1-b2ff-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6WB27W.jpg">© Kenzo Tribouillard, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Paris police officers go on trial over 2020 beating of Black man</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261109-paris-police-officers-go-on-trial-over-2020-beating-of-black-man</link><description>
Three French police officers went on trial Monday over the 2020 beating of Black music producer Michel Zecler in Paris. The assault, which was captured on camera, sparked nationwide outrage and renewed scrutiny of police violence and racism in France.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dba8d6a2-dc23-11f1-9698-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6VU4CT.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dba8d6a2-dc23-11f1-9698-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6VU4CT.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">476e3e4a-dc24-11f1-9f04-f3d8b2b0702c</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 10:08:03 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dba8d6a2-dc23-11f1-9698-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6VU4CT.jpg">© Thomas Samson, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French students vow to continue protests despite concessions from Macron govt</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261026-macron-vows-concrete-measures-to-address-student-demands-after-unrest</link><description>
French student leaders on Monday called for more protests despite President Emmanuel Macron's pledge of  "concrete and strong" measures to address their demands after weeks of nationwide unrest. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu met with high school representatives alongside education ministers to announce follow-up action ranging from a total overhaul of higher education admissions platform Parcoursup to a cap on class sizes.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ade564d2-d134-11f1-9bc8-6d20ccb9a352</guid><pubDate>Mon, 26 Oct 2026 12:25:21 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg">© Aurelien Morissard, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Focus</category><title>How the French army trains for 'high-intensity' combat</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/focus/20210714-how-the-french-army-trains-for-high-intensity-conflict</link><description>
France's new military programming law increases the country's defence budget to 2 percent of GDP by 2025. It's an investment in the modernisation of equipment, but also in the training of soldiers. The aim is to teach soldiers to face an army at least as well equipped as that of France in a context of global rearmament. Our reporters Fadile Bhayat, Mandi Heshmati and Caroline Grandjean followed French troops during a "high-intensity" training exercise.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/19df5ade-e4b0-11eb-b526-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/Focus%2014%20juillet.jpeg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/19df5ade-e4b0-11eb-b526-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/Focus%2014%20juillet.jpeg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">023ce07e-e41d-11eb-a94a-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Wed, 14 Jul 2021 14:42:34 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Fadile BHAYAT</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Macron says 'racist terrorist attack’ in Trappes marks turning point for France</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261023-french-prosecutors-investigate-paris-shooting-as-suspected-terror-attack</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron described Friday’s drive-by shooting in the western suburb of Trappes as a “terrorist and racist attack”, saying it marks a turning point for France. One person was killed and at least four people, including a 12-year-old girl, were wounded in the shooting, apparently at random. Two of the victims have immigrant backgrounds.

Et si vous appreniez que votre réseau social favori avait accès à vos informations personnelles sans votre autorisation ? C'est ce qu'il se serait produit en Italie depuis 2023. Les photos et vidéos d'environ 20 millions d'utilisateurs de Facebook auraient pu être consultés par la plateforme sans que cette dernière n'y ait été explicitement autorisée. Ainsi, samedi 14 novembre, l'autorité de protection des données personnelles italienne a lourdement sanctionné Meta, propriétaire de Facebook.

Invité aux Assises européennes du journalisme à Strasbourg, Kirill Martynov, cofondateur et rédacteur en chef de la rédaction sœur Novaïa Gazeta Europe basée à Riga, retrace l'histoire de ce média et détaille ses méthodes de travail qui ont fait exister le journalisme là où il est empêché. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/769103f0-df68-11f1-accb-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/Kirill-Martynov-Novaya-Gazeta-Europe-Assises-Strasbourg-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/769103f0-df68-11f1-accb-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/Kirill-Martynov-Novaya-Gazeta-Europe-Assises-Strasbourg-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">30a17c9c-df6f-11f1-8db3-d1351ad115d4</guid><pubDate>Sat, 14 Nov 2026 06:00:24 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Steven Jambot</dc:creator></item><item><category>Reportage international</category><title>Ukraine: à Lozova, des déplacés traumatisés par l'évacuation de la région de Donetsk</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/reportage-international/20261113-ukraine-%C3%A0-lozova-des-d%C3%A9plac%C3%A9s-traumatis%C3%A9s-par-l-%C3%A9vacuation-de-la-r%C3%A9gion-de-donetsk</link><description>
Dans l'est de l'Ukraine, l'évacuation des civils s'accélère face à l'intensification des combats dans la région de Donetsk. Selon les chiffres partagés par les autorités ukrainiennes, pendant les dix premiers jours de novembre, plus de 6 300 habitants ont quitté la région, dont 4 500 dans la seule communauté de Kramatorsk. À Droujkivka, les évacuations sont devenues extrêmement difficiles : une vingtaine de personnes seulement ont pu être évacuées depuis le début du mois. Quelques 340 civils se trouveraient toujours à Kostiantynivka. Dans la région voisine de Kharkiv, c'est à Lozova que ces personnes arrivent chaque jour par centaines. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/4c8900c2-df9e-11f1-9fb1-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/20261109-Centre-de-Transit-de-Lozova-RFI.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/4c8900c2-df9e-11f1-9fb1-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/20261109-Centre-de-Transit-de-Lozova-RFI.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">5d175c5c-df8c-11f1-9b2c-07b00a2c0fd8</guid><pubDate>Fri, 13 Nov 2026 23:07:17 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Emmanuelle Chaze</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Pourparlers sur l'Ukraine: un groupe de cinq pays se positionne pour représenter l'Europe</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261113-pourparlers-sur-l-ukraine-un-groupe-de-cinq-pays-se-positionne-pour-repr%C3%A9senter-l-europe</link><description>
